Daily Brief

The day's headlines are dominated by escalating tensions over energy and conflict. President Trump's announcement of a Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' has drawn sharp criticism from Kyiv, with President Zelensky reporting Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities continued despite the deal [BBC, Globe and Mail, The Hindu]. Trump also faces bipartisan backlash over plans to import Russian diesel to ease prices driven by the Iran war [BBC]. In the Middle East, Saudi Arabia extended the closure of Riyadh's main airport following deadly Houthi missile strikes that killed at least 18 people, with the kingdom's energy minister vowing a 'serious response' [BBC, Globe and Mail, The Hindu]. The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to South African jurist Navi Pillay, who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza—a decision likely to provoke controversy [Guardian]. Meanwhile, US economists Robert Hall and Michael Woodford received the Nobel in Economics for work on macroeconomic stabilization models now used by central banks worldwide [Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail]. In France, a 14-year-old student was arrested after shooting two teachers at a school in Aubagne, though injuries were not life-threatening [BBC, RFI].

Top Stories
01 Conflict

Trump's 'Energy Ceasefire' Between Russia and Ukraine Disputed as Strikes Continue

  • President Trump announced Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate 'energy ceasefire' halting strikes on each other's energy infrastructure
  • Ukrainian President Zelensky said he learned of the deal through media reports and that Russia struck multiple Ukrainian energy facilities—including a Kharkiv power plant—after the announcement
  • The Kremlin declined to confirm any ceasefire agreement, with spokesman Dmitry Peskov stating only that 'contacts are ongoing'
  • Trump separately announced Russia would supply millions of tonnes of diesel to global markets, drawing criticism from US lawmakers and Ukraine

03 Society

Nobel Peace Prize Awarded to Navi Pillay, Who Led UN Inquiry Finding Israel Guilty of Genocide

  • The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Peace Prize to South African jurist Navi Pillay for 'showing that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence'
  • Pillay chaired the UN commission that concluded in 2025 that Israel committed genocidal acts in Gaza with intent to destroy Palestinians
  • Israel refused to cooperate with the commission, called it biased, and rejected its findings as 'scandalous'
  • The committee cited Pillay's career including defending Nelson Mandela and serving as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights

04 Economics

Nobel Economics Prize Goes to Robert Hall and Michael Woodford for Macroeconomic Stabilization Models

  • US economists Robert Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences
  • The laureates developed models incorporating household and business decisions that are now used by central banks and governments worldwide
  • The Swedish Academy noted the models help authorities respond to economic shocks such as energy crises
  • Woodford emphasized that stabilization policy must account for how people understand and respond to policy decisions

05 Society

14-Year-Old Student Shoots Two Teachers at French School; Suspect Arrested

  • A 14-year-old ninth-grade student brought a shotgun concealed in a guitar case to Lakanal middle school in Aubagne, southern France
  • The principal, 53, and a teacher, 37, were shot and treated for non-life-threatening injuries; no children were harmed
  • A staff member restrained the student in a school corridor before police took him into custody
  • Local officials said the incident was not believed to be connected to ongoing protests over school conditions
